summary:
FAR FROM HOME — The Museum Nobody Can Visit

Since the 1960s, NASA has left more than 40 machines across the Moon, Mars, and deep space — from rovers that finished their missions to probes still whispering back from beyond the Solar System. Their stories are scattered across mission archives, invisible to the school-age space enthusiasts who would love them most. FAR FROM HOME turns this "abandoned" hardware into an interactive museum: 14 exhibits, each a museum placard showing the machine's live distance from Earth, one-way light time, and its current status (still talking / silent / crashed / deorbited). Every placard explains the science its exhibit made possible, from lunar laser ranging proving the Moon drifts 3.8 cm/year from Earth, to Opportunity's 45 km marathon, to Voyager 1 crossing a full light-day from home. Live imagery is pulled from the official NASA Image and Video Library API, so visitors see real mission photos. A postcard generator lets kids send shareable postcards from the edge of the solar system with real physics in every line. 

Impact: it converts forgotten hardware into a STEM gateway. It's a fully working, zero-install, mobile-friendly web experience that any classroom can open in a browser.
details:
• Approach: Researched NASA's NSSDCA Master Catalog and mission pages to select 14 exhibits spanning all three challenge environments (Moon, Mars, deep space) and all functionality states (active, silent, crashed, deorbited). Each exhibit was distilled into a "museum placard": mission dates, location, status, and the science it enabled, written for a school-age reading level.
  • Live data layer: Distance displays are computed in-browser — mean lunar distance; a simplified Mars orbital model (circular coplanar orbits, opposition-referenced) giving real-time Earth–Mars distance and light time; and Voyager 1's distance extrapolated from NASA's "Voyager Light-Day" milestone (173 AU, Aug 2025) at 3.57 AU/yr.
  • NASA imagery: Each exhibit fetches live imagery from the NASA Image and Video Library API (images-api.nasa.gov) at runtime; graceful monogram fallback if offline.
  • Tools & tech: Single-file HTML/CSS/JS (no build step, no dependencies) → deployable to GitHub Pages or Netlify in under a minute. Vanilla JavaScript, responsive grid layout, CSS starfield animations.
  • Solution development: Prototype → content research → interaction layer (filters, live ticks, postcard generator) → presentation polish, iterated against the five judging criteria.
